title: POC weekly latency tuning - Rivermark
summary: Weekly POC sync reviewing latency runs. Team validated TTFT improvements from streaming + kernel switch; still seeing tail latency spikes on long sequences. SE recommended kernel / perf flags, KV cache warm-up strategy, and batching tweaks. Agreed next steps: run new benchmark with optimized kernels, provide profiler traces, schedule on-prem test in 2 weeks, and share security docs for private deployment path.
action_items: Tom Becker: share kernel selection command lines and perf flags (due 2027-08-26)
Lena Ortiz: run 10k qps simulated workload with new flags and upload logs (due 2027-08-31)
Aisha Khan: send updated pricing and security docs for Private option (due 2027-08-27)
Jamal Rivera: schedule on-prem pilot slot with infra team for 2027-09-07 (due 2027-08-30)
next_steps: Run benchmark with kernel flags + streaming enabled and report TTFT/99th latency
Share perf traces and kernel logs (NVIDIA profiling + runtime logs)
Customer to validate KV-cache warm-up script on staging
Schedule on-prem pilot and provide list of required AMIs/containers
transcript:
[00:00] Aisha Khan: hey everybody thanks for joining, we'll try to keep to 45 minutes. quick roll call?
[00:05] Lena Ortiz: Lena here, hi. Mark here.
[00:07] Mark Chen: yep Mark, Evan is also on.
[00:09] Evan Ross: Evan on SRE.
[00:12] Tom Becker: Tom from Redwood, SE. Jamal on the line too.
[00:15] Priya Singh: Priya joining. Great thanks.

[02:10] Aisha Khan: quick agenda — results from last week's runs, TTFT focus, streaming outcomes, kernel selection, then action items. Lena you had some numbers?
[02:22] Lena Ortiz: yeah fwiw we re-ran the test with the streaming patch you sent, and we saw TTFT drop from around 220ms to ~140ms median for short prompts (128 tokens) which is nice. but the 95th and 99th were still around 550 to 820 ms so tails are concerning. also for sequences at 1024 tokens the average per-token latency increased and the end-to-end response time spiked.

[05:30] Tom Becker: okay that maps to what we expected — streaming reduces initial decode overhead but if kernels aren't the best fit for long sequences you still get tail spikes. we switched your runtime to the new fused-attn kernel on the 3090-like cluster — that helped on small seqs but long sequences still hit mem-bound kernels.

[06:12] Mark Chen: do you mean the fused mha kernel? sometimes our infra reports look like it falls back to the generic matmul kernel.
[06:22] Tom Becker: exactly, sometimes due to sequence length or KV cache layout the runtime picks the reference matmul. we have a couple of flags to force the optimized kernel when it's safe; we sent the command lines in the ticket but we can paste them here.

[07:00] Lena Ortiz: can forcing the kernel cause correctness issues? we can't risk hallucinations or degradation.
[07:07] Tom Becker: good question — on the model variants you're testing (redwood-compat-13b q4_0), the optimized kernels are validated; the risk is primarily numerical tiny differences but nothing that should change outputs semantically. we did QA across our prompt set.

[09:30] Evan Ross: i'm still worried about cold-starts — on warm nodes we see low latency but with autoscale new nodes add large TTFT. any guidance?
[09:45] Jamal Rivera: we recommend a KV-cache warm-up that can be run as part of scale-up hooks. basically pre-populate prefix encodings for common prompts so that first real request doesn't pay full cost. it's a small script; we can share.

[11:20] Lena Ortiz: we tried a smaller warm-up snippet but maybe we didn't do a good job of covering the prompt shapes. will try a more representative set.

[12:45] Tom Becker: also batching matters — your current bursty pattern has small batches which increases per-token overhead. streaming plus continuous batching can help but you need to tune max latency budgets so a request doesn't wait too long.

[14:05] Priya Singh: can you share what kind of throughput improvements we should expect if we enable continuous batching? our SLA target is 200ms P50 and 700ms P99 for the assistant.

[14:25] Tom Becker: rough numbers from similar customers: continuous batching with 8-12ms collection windows with streaming trimmed P50 significantly and sometimes improved cost per token by 20-30% while keeping P99 within 600-800ms depending on model and seq len. for you with shorter prompts you should hit P50 ~120-160ms after optimizations, P99 is the harder one.

[16:00] Lena Ortiz: we also noticed sequence length distribution is bimodal — 70% short (<=128) and 30% long (>512). is there a recommended policy to route long sequences to a different model variant?

[16:18] Tom Becker: yes — smart routing can help: route short sequences to the low-latency quantized kernel instance and long ones to a variant optimized for throughput (bigger batch sizes and different memory layout). Redwood's routing policy can do that; there's a config snippet.

[18:05] Mark Chen: any tradeoffs on quantization here? we're using q4_0 now. would q6 or q8 help latency?

[18:18] Jamal Rivera: quantization level impacts both quality and kernel choices. q6 sometimes needs different kernel paths and may increase kernel compute time on certain GPUs, but reduces memory pressure, which helps with long sequences. we recommended testing q6 model on a small subset.

[20:45] Lena Ortiz: on the last run we tried q6 and saw slightly worse median but better tail in some cases, but it's noisy. we need more runs.

[22:00] Tom Becker: for the kernel selection — i'm going to send three commands: 1) force fused-attn, 2) prefer tiled-gemm for seq > 512, 3) enable prefetch for KV layout. together those brought down your 99th from 820 to ~620 in our internal tests.

[23:12] Priya Singh: what about cost? if we force optimized kernels and keep nodes warm, will our monthly spend spike?

[23:25] Aisha Khan: good point — median improvements often reduce token compute cost, but keeping warm nodes increases fixed spend. we can model hybrid: keep a small warm pool for peak windows and rely on hosted bursting as backup. Jamal can follow up with a cost model.

[25:50] Mark Chen: security / private deployment questions — if we move to Private, how do we get KMS and audit logs integrated? any downtime for migration?

[26:05] Jamal Rivera: Private supports customer-managed KMS and syslog/audit forwarding. migration typically is blue/green with no customer downtime; we replicate the config and switch traffic. we will share the security docs Aisha mentioned.

[27:30] Lena Ortiz: for profiling, what traces do you need? we have nsight dumps and some runtime logs.

[27:40] Tom Becker: nsight is great. we'll want kernel timelines, per-layer mem traces, and Redwood runtime logs showing kernel selection decisions. please scrub any PII. we use those to tune fallbacks.

[29:10] Evan Ross: one more — we saw occasional OOMs when parallel requests with long sequences come in; any quick mitigations?

[29:22] Jamal Rivera: short-term we suggest request-level limits (max tokens) and a queueing policy; medium-term is move long seqs to a larger instance type or switch to tiled kernels that are less memory-hungry.

[31:00] Aisha Khan: let's recap. Tom will share kernel commands and perf flags; Jamal will share KV warm-up script and cost model; Lena will run benchmark with new flags and upload logs; Aisha will send security and pricing docs and schedule the on-prem pilot slot.

[31:40] Tom Becker: i'll paste the three kernel flags in the follow-up message: --kernel=fused_attn --prefer=tiled_gemm:seq_gt_512 --kv-prefetch=on. note these are runtime flags for the Redwood runtime image.

[33:50] Lena Ortiz: one question — could streaming cause partial outputs that confuse downstream tool callers? we do have a toolchain that expects full JSON.

[34:05] Tom Becker: yes streaming can emit intermediate chunks; we recommend structured chunk boundaries and using message-complete hooks. Redwood supports function-calling style that buffers until complete JSON is emitted or emits final chunk. we can enable structured-output mode.

[36:00] Mark Chen: please include example config for function-calling mode.

[36:12] Jamal Rivera: will do.

[38:00] Priya Singh: timeline wise we'd like to decide on dedicated vs private by the end of next quarter. we need numbers for cost and latency tradeoffs.

[38:15] Aisha Khan: understood; we'll prioritize the benchmark and cost model this week.

[40:00] Lena Ortiz: ok we'll aim to run the 10k qps sim and post results by 8/31.

[41:30] Aisha Khan: great — last call before the on-prem pilot then. Any final quick notes?

[42:10] Evan Ross: none from SRE.

[42:20] Mark Chen: nadda.

[42:30] Priya Singh: thanks everyone.

[42:40] Tom Becker: thanks all, follow-up email with commands and links.

[42:50] Aisha Khan: end.
